sections.title: Introduction
sections.job: 2pp. Orient a blind reader: the broad spectral problem; the acquired overlap record; ITQDE minimally; Z_tau(s) as the primary object; the staircase as a derived readout; the general method separated from the subset-sum benchmark; a short roadmap. ONE narrow claim stated from the start (the measured overlaps are independent of the target and support a range of resolutions) - no defensive corrections, no triple qualification of the same claim. The claim-status table wording matches the body exactly (the compressibility statement is a proposition under a generic spacing estimate and a prethermal approximation, never a proved structural result). No editorial debris about earlier drafts or retired terminology. Written LAST per body_lock_order.
sections.notes: Judgement L190-230: the intro treats orientation as solved by adding labels; reduce the apparatus load. Figure NF1 (general architecture + generic example, full width) is this section's one figure.

sections.title: Relation to ITQDE and record-based spectral methods
sections.job: 2-3pp. The parent ITQDE construction, then the method located against nearby approaches BY TASK: pole recovery; spectral-distribution estimation; subspace/Krylov methods; coherent filter synthesis; reusable statistical records. A technical comparison - no contest rhetoric, no 'furthest any prior method goes', and NO re-introduction of the method the introduction already defined. Carry the real Prony contrast: pole recovery attempts an inverse problem that conditions badly in dense noisy spectra, while SSG computes regularised linear spectral functionals at a chosen scale - controlled resolution bought by giving up exact line recovery. The exact moment identities are properties of any Gaussian-smoothed spectral measure, not a novelty boundary: the contribution is the acquisition-and-reuse architecture plus the finite-record analysis. Peaked-circuit / XEB / benchmarking material does not belong here.

sections.title: Spectral Surface Generation
sections.job: The general method. Open with the input-output contract (H; probe; bandwidth bound; measured Ghat(t_k); supported (s,tau) domain; reconstructed Zhat_tau(s)), then derive the transform. Finite reconstruction notationally distinct (Zhat_{tau,m} vs Z_tau; 'exact' reserved for the continuous transform and algebraic identities). Heat-kernel scale-space stated forward-stable: coarser representations are stable, finer scales require longer and more accurate real-time data - never 'the same equation run backward'. Response identities with the corrected first cumulant. The classical algorithm priced under an explicit query model (oracle per (s,tau) / discretised grid / FFT bulk transform per tau). The moment hierarchy costed: no new quantum observable, but higher moments need larger shot budgets or stronger regularisation. Kernel generalisations beyond the Gaussian get ONE paragraph (reweighting by other time-domain kernels within the acquired support) - no non-Hermitian second paper.
sections.notes: Judgement L276-396. After the record is acquired, changing s, tau, or a coefficient insertion requires no further quantum evolution - that is the claim; 'one measurement' never appears.

sections.title: Acquisition and the finite-record envelope
sections.job: Causal order, not nine subsections: measurement primitive -> bandwidth and time grid (the grid constant derived or its ITQDE inheritance named, never bare 'Nyquist') -> maximum time and truncation (t_max = 2*sqrt(tau*log(1/eps_w)) everywhere, code convention agreeing) -> one-sided record reduction and symmetric branches (one time convention) -> shot-noise propagation -> the supported (s,tau) domain -> optional observable branches and symmetry diagnostics. The visibility story carries the derived finite-shot covariance result for shared-record ratio estimators, and every claim about reading exponentially small weight is sized to that derivation.
sections.notes: Judgement L398-491. Figure NF2 (finite-record envelope) lives here.

sections.title: The controlled subset-sum embodiment
sections.job: One section: encoding, exact product control, noncommuting diagnostics, decoder. The instance is encoded in H0, not the probe; state IMMEDIATELY that at production scale a_i = O(n^2) dynamic programming is polynomial (pseudo-polynomially tractable benchmark - no worst-case NP-hardness inheritance). Exact product control with the corrected 2^-n normalisation, named 'exact Fourier coefficient collapse' (no circle-method grandeur). The perturbative fingerprint under its stated forward model: the response depends on P_S V P_S, solution geometry and probe weights - never a universal function of g; the null channel carries its finite empirical floor; the free-fermion selection rule is derived, not asserted as 'nothing to split'. Degeneracy cartography and the integer decoder presented as estimation followed by constrained decoding, with the crossing-displacement assumptions attached to the equation, chain error propagated, the erasure rule honest (erased stays erased), and the benchmark's tiny hypothesis class (max degeneracy two) stated as the controlled test it is.
sections.notes: Judgement L493-628. Figures NF3 (subset-sum control), NF4 (perturbative response), and the DP benchmark table live here.

sections.title: Numerical validation
sections.job: Evidence separated and TYPED every time: exact algebra evaluated numerically / exact diagonalisation (n<=12) / synthetic finite-shot sampling / TEBD (n<=20); no quantum hardware data exists in this paper. The reference validates the reconstruction against a classically computed model under trusted assumptions - 'certification' does not appear. Route agreement between two reconstruction routes on one bank is an implementation consistency check and lives in the appendix; the exact-zero tau-dial error is a unit test by construction. Tested sizes are proof-of-principle, never asymptotic scaling laws. Decoder performance reported as coverage, conditional accuracy, and full-profile recovery with uncertainty.
sections.notes: Judgement L630-659. Figures NF5 (decoder performance) and NF6 (operating envelope + finite-size simulation cost) live here or in N7 per the figure leg.

sections.title: Limits and discussion
sections.job: Three movements. (1) The generic finite-size result at its earned strength: for tested distinct-weight instances and couplings inside the readable window, MPS bond dimension stays small and roughly n-independent, with the perturbative explanation - and the derivation chain sized per the blocking-issue resolutions (denominator assumption stated, many-body norm correct, prethermal timescale compared to t_max(tau), quasi-local rotation's entanglement cost acknowledged). (2) The planted construction: readability and growing MPS cost coexist over the tested range; chi growth is consistent with exponential over tested sizes (a guide, not an established law); the Jt clock is costed through the acquisition ledger. (3) The open hardness question stated as open. Sign-problem material at most one paragraph. No unconditional complexity language anywhere.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.job: Half a page, three paragraphs: (1) a precise statement of the general method; (2) what the benchmark demonstrated and what its limitations were; (3) what remains open. No re-argument of the manuscript, no repeated introduction, no resonant closer. Written after the body and appendices lock, before title/abstract/introduction.

appendices.title: Disclosure crosswalk and exactness taxonomy
appendices.job: A reference apparatus, not an argument - and it behaves that way throughout. The five-column crosswalk (Technical element | Paper definition | Supporting result | Evidence type | Conditions) over CANDIDATE disclosure elements (never 'independent claims'), with coarse rows split into separable elements (acquisition; storage; post-acquisition s; post-acquisition tau; reconstruction; derived moments; observable branches). The seven-category exactness taxonomy: Exact identity / Controlled approximation / Numerical implementation check / Synthetic finite-shot study / Benchmark-specific inference / Candidate embodiment / Open complexity claim. No naming history, no 'as of this draft' commentary, no persuasion, no science that is not in the body; 'no visibility floor' does not survive as an element.
